fields.explore_cta: Build My Potluck Sign Up Sheet
fields.features_heading: What the Sheet Handles Once People Sign Up
fields.features_subheading: A potluck sign up sheet lists who brings which dish. These six parts keep every course covered and every cook reminded.
fields.feature_1:
Slots per course that close when full

Sets a number of slots for mains, sides, desserts, and drinks. Once a course is full, it drops off the list, and the next guest sees only the courses that still need a dish.
fields.feature_2:
An allergen box on every dish

Asks each cook to tick what the dish contains, such as tree nuts or dairy. The host gets one list of the tagged dishes and can label each one on the table before guests arrive.
fields.feature_3:
Servings counted against the guest list

Asks each household for its headcount and how many people its dish feeds. Servings are totaled by course against the headcount, and a short course shows up before anyone shops.
fields.feature_4:
A reminder email the day before

Emails every guest who signed up on the evening before the event, with the dish they chose and the drop-off time. Set the send time and the wording when you describe the sheet.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Shows one question per screen, so a guest opening the link from a group text can pick a course and name a dish without any zooming. Each sign-up is saved once submitted.
fields.feature_6:
Sign-ups in a database you own

Keeps every sign-up in a database you own instead of a paper grid taped to the break room fridge. On paid plans, export the full code of the sheet to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: What the Sheet Did at Four Potlucks
fields.tab_content_1:
Sides close when all 6 slots fill

Wendeline Pruett runs the Thanksgiving potluck at the Ferrowby Freight office and splits the sheet into 4 mains, 6 sides, 4 desserts, and 2 drinks. When all 6 side slots are claimed, sides close. Ludovic Brevard signs up next, sees only mains, desserts, and drinks, and picks pumpkin pie.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each nut dish named in one email to the kitchen

Calderbrook Community Church serves a Christmas dinner after its evening service, and 18 cooks sign up to bring a dish. Each cook ticks tree nuts, dairy, eggs, or gluten. Kitchen lead Mirela Dobrescu gets one email listing the 3 dishes with tree nuts, and she sets them on a separate table.
fields.tab_content_3:
22 households, each emailed its dish the night before

Bastian Haldane closes Thistlewood Lane for a Halloween block party, and 22 households sign up with a dish. At 6 pm the evening before, each one gets an email naming its dish and the 5:30 pm drop-off. The Sorensby household's email reads caramel apples.
fields.tab_content_4:
Short on mains by 14 servings, the organizer gets an alert

Agathe Ebbesen is planning a reunion for 62 relatives. Each household enters its headcount, its dish, and how many people the dish feeds. Once all 19 households sign up, mains cover 48 servings, fewer than the headcount. Agathe gets an email that mains are short by 14. Sides and desserts cover everyone.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Potluck Sign-Up Sheet
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a potluck sign up sheet that covers every course and reminds every cook, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Count the guests before the dishes
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Split the menu into course slots
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Plan for food that sits out
fields.howto_step_1_des: Get a headcount first from the RSVP replies, and write it at the top of your plan. Every later number comes from that one count, including the slots per course and how many servings each dish should feed the guests who said yes.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide how many dishes each course needs, and cap every course. For 30 guests, try 5 mains, 8 sides, 4 desserts, and 3 drinks. Add 2 slots for plates and ice, and assign them like any other dish on the sheet.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a checkbox list of allergens, such as tree nuts and dairy, plus a line for anything else. A guest with an allergy can read the sheet before the event instead of asking every cook at the table which dish is safe to eat.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A University of Florida IFAS extension post says to discard all perishable foods that have been left at room temperature for more than 2 hours. Set the drop-off time close to serving, and put the cold dishes out last.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt that names each course with its slot count, asks the allergen question, and says who hears about a short course. Emergent builds the sheet and the database behind it. Change any part later by asking, such as adding a drinks slot.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick when the reminder goes out, such as the morning of the event, and what it says: the dish and the drop-off address. Guests who signed up three weeks earlier get their own dish back in writing, with time left to shop.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign up three times yourself, once into a course that is nearly full, and check that the course closes and the reminder names the right dish. Delete the test rows before anyone else signs up, then share the link in the group text.

faq_plan.q: What is a potluck sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: A potluck sign up sheet is a list where guests claim the dish they will bring to a shared meal. It tells the host what is covered before the day. A good one caps each course and records who brings what.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a potluck sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Count your guests, split the menu into courses with a cap on each, and decide what every cook should tell you about their dish. Then describe it to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the sheet, the database of sign-ups, and the reminder emails. Share it as a link in the invitation or the group text.

faq_plan.q: What should a potluck sign up sheet template include?
faq_plan.a: Six fields cover it: name, course, dish, servings, allergens, and an email for the reminder. Put the date and the drop-off time at the top. Emergent builds the template from a plain-English description, and any field can be changed later by asking.

faq_plan.q: How do you plan a thanksgiving potluck sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Assign the turkey before the sheet goes out, and nobody signs up to roast a second one. Then open slots for stuffing, potatoes, cranberry sauce, rolls, and pies. If seats at the table are limited, collect names with a registration form first and send the sheet only to the people who registered.

faq_plan.q: What dishes belong on a christmas potluck sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Put a ham or a roast in mains, then sides that hold well, cookies and pie in desserts, and a hot drink. Ask for a slow cooker or chafing dish for each hot main: food safety guidance from the University of Florida says hot foods need to be held at 140 degrees F or above.

faq_plan.q: What are good ideas for a halloween potluck sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Give the courses themed names, such as Monster Mains and Graveyard Desserts, and leave the dish itself to the cook. Add a slot for candy for trick-or-treaters and one for a pumpkin dip. If children will be there, ask every cook to tick tree nuts and the other allergens their dish contains.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a potluck sign up sheet online free?
faq_plan.ref: potluck sign up sheet online free
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing a potluck sign up sheet, with no cap on how many guests sign up. Share the link by text or email, and every sign-up lands in a database you own. For a paid event with sessions and badges, a conference registration form fits better.

faq_plan.q: How do I run a holiday potluck sign up sheet at work?
faq_plan.a: Post the sheet two weeks ahead, and cap each course by the office headcount. Ask who needs fridge or oven space on the day, and set the drop-off before lunch. Every sign-up from a sheet Emergent builds sits in a database the office owns, and next year's list can start from this one.

faq_plan.q: What goes on a christmas party sign up sheet besides food?
faq_plan.a: Add the jobs that make the party run: setup, decorations, music, the gift exchange, and cleanup. Give each job a time and a number of people, such as 3 people for cleanup at 9 pm. If there is a gift exchange, put the price limit at the top of the sheet.

faq_plan.q: Can a food sign up sheet template work for a camp or club?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep the course slots and the allergen boxes, and add a field for the camper's or member's name. The same food sign up sheet template then covers a camp cookout or a club banquet. If families also enroll children for the season, handle that with a summer camp registration form and keep the food sheet for the cookout.

plan.angle: The top 10 for potluck sign up sheet is printable grids and generic slot sign-up tools: a list of blank lines, or slots someone has to fill in by hand. This page shows what the sheet does once people start signing up, in four gatherings searchers run: an office Thanksgiving potluck whose side-dish slots close at 6, a church Christmas dinner where each cook tags allergens, a Halloween block party where every household gets a reminder the evening before, and a family reunion where the organizer hears that mains fall short of the headcount. The FAQ covers templates, Thanksgiving, Christmas, Halloween and holiday sheets, free online options and what a party sheet holds besides food.
